findings.title: Header panel loses right alignment in IE10's flexbox implementation
findings.body: The previous `float: right` is removed, and the only main-axis positioning now is `margin-left: auto`. IE10's `-ms-flexbox` implementation does not distribute auto margins on flex items; since a child float is ignored once `.contents` becomes a flex container, the panel will sit immediately after the title/extra-info instead of at the right edge. The new mixin explicitly emits `-ms-flexbox`, so provide a legacy-compatible spacer/flex-growth or alignment rule for that implementation.

findings.title: The legacy Firefox flex fallback has no alignment property
findings.body: `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for Firefox versions using the legacy box model, but `align-items()` emits only `-webkit-box-align` for legacy box alignment and omits `-moz-box-align`. Those Firefox versions therefore ignore every `@include align-items(...)` call and use the default stretch alignment, leaving the new header and small-action layouts uncentered and bullet badges unaligned. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment` alongside the WebKit legacy declaration.
